blocking_issues: Number_of_Responsible_Persons is mapped directly to entity.responsible_person_count, but the user guide (p. 3, §22) explicitly says a source value of zero means the charity did not supply this information. Emitting zero as a count would create a false claim that the charity has zero responsible persons. Add a condition excluding zero or leave this field unmapped; the current mapping has no such condition.

Operating_Countries is mapped without qualification to entity.operating_country, whose supplied definition is for a country code reported for an overseas operating location. Raw discovery shows AUS for charities whose business addresses are in Australia (including the supplied SJD Homes, North West Regional Landcarers, Catholic Cemeteries, and Delatite examples). AUS cannot be an overseas location for these Australian charity records. The disclosed uncertainty does not prevent the mapping from emitting a semantically misleading canonical observation. Exclude the unsupported AUS case or leave the field unmapped unless source semantics supporting this concept are established.
warnings: The legal-name mapping, ACNC-specific registration-date mapping, and separate establishment-date mapping preserve distinct meanings supported by the guide. No current/historic name conflation is evident; Other_Organisation_Names is conservatively left unmapped, with its mixed trading/other-name semantics disclosed.

The source describes a charity record and explicitly associates it with a charity ABN and formal legal/official name. Treating the row as a legal-entity subject is reasonable on the supplied evidence; no reporting-group field is being asserted.

The business-address components and Address_Type mapping are supported by the documentation and samples. Operating-region, subtype, and beneficiary indicator mappings use affirmative Y values and do not turn blanks into negative claims.

No legal-entity status is inferred from inclusion in the ACNC register, and ACNC registration date is not misrepresented as company registration date. Omitting unsupported status, company identifiers, licences, and historic-name claims is acceptable.

The publication-proxy timestamp policy is disclosed and allowed by the supplied engine semantics. The website quarantine example is a disclosed data-quality limitation, not a semantic blocker. Confidence values are judgements and do not remedy the two semantic issues above.
evidence_checked: ACNC dataset notes: registered-charities subset, weekly updates, voluntary ACNC registration context, and withholding caveats.
ACNC user guide p. 1 §§2–5: dataset comprises charities registered with ACNC and is based on multiple sources; records may be withheld.
ACNC user guide p. 2 §§6–17: charity ABN, formal/legal name, other names, business address, website, and effective ACNC registration-date definitions.
ACNC user guide p. 3 §§18–24: establishment date; charity-size source and blank meaning; responsible-person count, including explicit zero sentinel; financial-year end.
ACNC user guide pp. 4–6 §§25–34: operating-region indicators, Operating_Countries ISO alpha-3 explanation, subtype indicators, beneficiary indicators.

Supplied raw discovery records: Australian charity names and business addresses with Operating_Countries values AUS; records also include nonzero responsible-person counts, while the documentation establishes zero semantics.

Mapping fields, filters, transformations, unmapped fields, confidence, and limitations; in particular, no zero filter on responsible-person count and no condition excluding AUS from operating_country.
Supplied ontology definitions and trusted engine semantics for operating_country, integer conversion, subject roles, publication proxy, and canonical claims.

blocking_issues: Charity_Legal_Name is mapped unconditionally to entity.legal_name, but the source guide expressly says that where a charity's legal name is withheld, ACNC may substitute an alternate identifier in this field. The map therefore makes a legal-name claim for values that the source says may not be legal names. No discriminator, exclusion, or limitation addresses these records. This needs a safe treatment (for example, avoid making the legal-name claim where the value cannot be verified as a legal name, if the source provides a usable discriminator) before the mapping is acceptable for human review.
warnings: The attempted exploration failed with NameError because `records` was undefined. Thus the stated one-row-per-charity grain and no-duplicate-ABN assumption were not checked across the full discovery sample. Supplied examples show distinct ABNs, and source notes describe charity-level fields, so this is an evidential gap rather than a demonstrated grain error.

Other_Organisation_Names is appropriately left unmapped: source meaning mixes trading names and other names, without guaranteeing each value is a trading name. Operating_Countries is also conservatively left unmapped given observed AUS values and the ontology's explicitly overseas-location scope.

No entity status is inferred from being registered in an ACNC dataset; the source is a current weekly subset but does not provide an entity-status field. ACNC registration date is correctly kept distinct from entity/company registration, and establishment date is separately mapped.

The business address is documented as the charity's business address and Address_Type samples say Business; address components are appropriately address-scoped, not service-location claims. Reported operating regions and charity indicators are entity-scoped claims, not address locations.

The mapped subtype and beneficiary categories are supported by the guide's named categories and Y-indicator semantics; blanks are not emitted as negative claims. The zero responsible-person sentinel is excluded as documented.
The confidence scores are provisional judgments, as disclosed. High scores on directly documented fields are not themselves a blocker; the legal-name semantic exception is the material issue.
evidence_checked: ACNC user guide p. 2 §§6–11: ABN is the charity's ABN; Charity name is formally the legal/official name, except that an alternate identifier may be substituted when the legal name is withheld; other organisation names may be trading names or other names.

ACNC user guide p. 2 §§12–17: address is the charity business address; website where supplied; registration date is effective ACNC registration date, including the stated 3 December 2012 convention for some pre-ACNC registrations.
ACNC user guide p. 3 §§18–24: establishment date, latest-AIS size categories and blank meaning, zero responsible-person sentinel, and financial year-end semantics.
ACNC user guide pp. 4–6 §§25–34: state/territory operating indicators, ISO alpha-3 overseas-country description, subtype indicators, and beneficiary indicators.

Raw discovery rows 2–9: distinct sample ABNs; Address_Type is Business; examples of legal-name and other-name separation; dates, operating indicators, subtype/beneficiary Y values, and Operating_Countries values including AUS.

Previous mapping and validation feedback: legal name is mapped without conditions; status and company-type claims are not inferred; website value Instagram was quarantined; exploration script failed before checking duplicate ABNs.
